Introduction

What Is a Section 8 Company?

A Section 8 Company is registered under the Companies Act, 2013, for promoting objects like commerce, art, science, education, charity or social welfare, with profits reinvested into those objects rather than distributed as dividends. It operates with a Central Government licence rather than the word "Limited" in its name.

This structure carries more governance rigour than a Trust, and is often preferred by organisations seeking institutional funding or CSR partnerships that expect a company-style structure.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Strong credibility with donors, CSR partners and institutions
  • Limited liability protection for members
  • Eligible for tax exemptions under 12A and 80G, subject to conditions
  • Separate legal entity with perpetual succession

Disadvantages

  • Profits cannot be distributed to members as dividends
  • Higher compliance burden than a Trust
  • Requires a Central Government licence before incorporation
  • Any change to objects requires regulatory approval

Eligibility

Who Can Register a Section 8 Company

  • Minimum 2 directors for a private Section 8 Company
  • A clearly defined non-profit object — charity, education, social welfare, etc.
  • A commitment that profits will be applied only toward the stated objects
  • A registered office address in India

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. DSC & Name Reservation

Obtain DSC for directors and reserve the company name via the RUN/SPICe+ service.

2. Drafting MOA & AOA

We draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting the company's non-profit objects.

3. Licence Application (Section 8)

Apply for the Section 8 licence from the Central Government (via the Regional Director) confirming the non-profit purpose.

4. Incorporation Filing

Once the licence is granted, file for incorporation with the ROC. Timelines can vary and typically run longer than a standard company due to the licence step.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN and address proof of all directors
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Proof of registered office (utility bill + NOC from owner)
  • A declaration of estimated income and expenditure for the next three years

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements After Registration

  • Annual ROC filing (AOC-4 & MGT-7)
  • Statutory audit of financial statements
  • Income tax return filing, and 12A/80G renewal where applicable
  • Board meetings as prescribed under the Companies Act
